chunks: Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ribʿī who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said to Yaḥyā al-Saqqāʾ: 'O Yaḥyā, verily good character is a means of ease, and verily bad character causes difficulty.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and practical impact of good versus bad character according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sādiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that ethical conduct is not merely a spiritual ideal but a practical determinant of worldly ease (*yusr*) versus hardship (*nakd*). This teaching aligns with the Shia tradition of *adab* (manners) as a tangible manifestation of faith, where inner piety directly influences one's external experience of life's challenges.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 6.Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ribʿī who said, “
Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) said to Yaḥyā al-Saqqāʾ, ‘O Yaḥyā, verily good character is a means of ease, and verily bad character causes difficulty.’”
